Doctor: Hello. Could you tell me your age and gender, and what brings you in today?
Patient: I'm 65 years old, and I'm a female. I've been dealing with iron deficiency anemia for a long time, and I came in because I was told I was anemic again when I tried to donate blood in December. I've been feeling really tired, having chills, and even some wheezing when I try to be active. It's been frustrating not knowing why this keeps happening.
Doctor: Could you provide more details about your dietary habits, including any changes in your intake of iron-rich foods or supplements, and whether you have a history of menstrual bleeding or gastrointestinal issues that might contribute to iron deficiency?
Patient: I don't have a history of menstrual bleeding anymore since I had a hysterectomy in 1996. As for my diet, I haven't really made any changes to eat more iron-rich foods, but I did start taking iron pills again about a year ago after not taking them for some time. I also take over-the-counter vitamin B12 supplements. I don't have any known gastrointestinal issues, but I do get cold easily and have been feeling more anxious and depressed lately.
Doctor: Could you provide details about any recent gastrointestinal symptoms, such as changes in bowel habits, abdominal pain, or black stools? Additionally, have you undergone any upper or lower gastrointestinal endoscopy or imaging studies to evaluate for potential sources of blood loss?
Patient: I don't have any changes in my bowel habits or abdominal pain, and I haven't noticed any black stools. I had a colonoscopy about five to six years ago, and it was normal with no polyps. They said to come back in 10 years, so I haven't had an upper endoscopy yet.
Doctor: Have you had any recent upper endoscopy or capsule endoscopy to evaluate for potential sources of chronic gastrointestinal blood loss, such as angiodysplasia or small bowel lesions?
Patient: No, I haven't had an upper endoscopy or capsule endoscopy yet. The doctor mentioned that if my initial tests come back normal, they might consider a capsule endoscopy to check for any issues in my digestive system that could be causing the anemia.
Doctor: Has the patient undergone any imaging studies of the small bowel, such as a capsule endoscopy or small bowel follow-through, to evaluate for potential sources of chronic blood loss, such as angiodysplasia or celiac disease?
Patient: No, I haven't had any imaging studies of the small bowel, like a capsule endoscopy or small bowel follow-through. reference_so.subjective:
Basic information: 65-year-old female with chief complaint of recurrent iron deficiency anemia, fatigue, chills, and wheezing on exertion.

History of present illness: Onset of symptoms not specified, but patient has a long-standing history of iron deficiency anemia. Recently confirmed anemic during blood donation in December. Symptoms include fatigue, chills, and wheezing with activity. Patient also mentions not making dietary changes to increase iron intake but restarting iron pills about a year ago and taking over-the-counter vitamin B12 supplements.

Past history: Iron deficiency anemia (long-standing), hysterectomy in 1996, use of iron pills for approximately one year, and over-the-counter vitamin B12 supplements. No known gastrointestinal issues. Personal history includes feelings of being cold, anxiety, and depression. No recent gastrointestinal evaluations such as capsule endoscopy or small bowel imaging. No capsule endoscopy or small bowel imaging performed. Celiac disease testing (tTG-IgA, EMA) not performed.
reference_so.objective:
Physical examination: Vital signs: Temperature 36.8°C, pulse 78 bpm, BP 120/80 mmHg, RR 16 breaths/min, SpO2 98% on room air. Physical examination reveals no jaundice, no palpable lymphadenopathy, no hepatosplenomegaly. Respiratory examination shows mild expiratory wheezing on auscultation. No signs of gastrointestinal bleeding or masses on abdominal examination.

Investigations: Hemoglobin: 9.2 g/dL (normal: 12-16 g/dL), MCV: 72 fL (microcytic), serum ferritin: 12 ng/mL (low), serum iron: 25 µg/dL (low), total iron-binding capacity (TIBC): 480 µg/dL (elevated), transferrin saturation: 5.2% (low). Chest X-ray: No acute infiltrates or cardiomegaly. Pulmonary function tests: Mild obstructive pattern with FEV1/FVC ratio of 0.65. Stool occult blood test: Negative. Upper endoscopy: No active bleeding or ulcers, but mild gastritis noted. Colonoscopy: No polyps or tumors, but mild diverticulosis noted. No prior small bowel imaging studies such as capsule endoscopy or small bowel follow-through performed. Celiac disease screening (tTG-IgA, EMA) not performed.
